title: 3D Integrability Infrastructure — Compact Box to Ioc Product
content: integrable_3d_zx_y proves that G((z,x),y) = f(x,y,z) is integrable on the triple Ioc product measure. The proof chain: (1) G is continuous (composition of f with a coordinate permutation); (2) G is integrableOn the compact Icc box [e,f']×[a,b]×[c,d]; (3) Two applications of restrict_prod_eq_prod_restrict convert Icc to an Icc product measure; (4) mono_measure transfers from Icc to Ioc (since Ioc ⊆ Icc). The permutation of arguments ((z,x),y) ↦ f(x,y,z) is what enables the outer integral swap in Step 2.
mathContext: For $f: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous, the function $G: ((z,x), y) \mapsto f(x,y,z)$ is integrable on the product measure $\mu_{[e,f']} \otimes \mu_{[a,b]} \otimes \mu_{[c,d]}$ (where $\mu_{[p,q]}$ is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(p,q]$). Key lemma used: `Integrable.integral_prod_right` — if $G$ is integrable on $\mu \otimes \nu$, then $(p \mapsto \int_{\nu} G(p, \cdot))$ is integrable on $\mu$. Applied to the 3D product, this gives integrability of $(z,x) \mapsto \int_y f(x,y,z)$, which is exactly what `MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap` requires.

title: Triple Fubini — 3-Step Transposition
content: triple_fubini_of_continuous proves ∫z∫y∫x f = ∫x∫y∫z f via three steps: (1) For each fixed z, swap (x,y) using the parent theorem GreensTheoremOQ01OQ01.fubini_of_continuous — this is a pointwise application using integral_congr; (2) Swap the outer (z,x) pair using integral_integral_swap on the Ioc set integrals — integrability comes from integrable_3d_zx_y + integral_prod_right; (3) For each fixed x, swap (y,z) using 2D Fubini again. The three steps compose to give the full (z,y,x) → (x,y,z) transposition.
mathContext: The 3-step proof: let $I_{zyx} = \int_z \int_y \int_x f$. (1) By 2D Fubini under $z$: $I_{zyx} = \int_z \int_x \int_y f = I_{zxy}$. (2) By `integral_integral_swap` ($\int_z \int_x h = \int_x \int_z h$ for integrable $h$): $I_{zxy} = I_{xzy}$. (3) By 2D Fubini under $x$: $I_{xzy} = \int_x \int_y \int_z f = I_{xyz}$. The key technical requirement for step (2) is: $(z,x) \mapsto \int_y f(x,y,z)$ is integrable on $\mu_z \otimes \mu_x$ — provided by `integrable_3d_zx_y.integral_prod_right`.

title: All Key Orderings Equal — Collecting the Results
content: triple_fubini_all_equal proves that three key orderings of ∫∫∫ f all equal the canonical (x,y,z) ordering. The proof is a straightforward composition: (z,y,x) = (x,y,z) is triple_fubini_of_continuous; (z,x,y) = (x,y,z) by first using 2D Fubini inside (reverse) then triple_fubini_of_continuous; (y,x,z) = (x,y,z) is triple_fubini_yxz_eq_xyz. Together these generators (12, 13, 23 transpositions) suffice to generate all 3! = 6 permutations of 3 variables.
mathContext: The symmetric group $S_3$ is generated by the adjacent transpositions $(12)$, $(23)$, and $(13)$: the three generators $\tau_{zyx \to xyz}$, $\tau_{zxy \to xyz}$, $\tau_{yxz \to xyz}$ established here correspond to compositions of these transpositions. Since $|S_3| = 6$ and any permutation of 3 elements can be written as a product of at most 3 transpositions, these three theorems (plus symmetry of `=`) give all 6 orderings. For $n > 3$, the pattern generalizes inductively: peel off the outermost variable, apply IH inside, use `integral_integral_swap` for each adjacent transposition in the outer variable.

title: iteratedIntervalIntegral — The n-Dimensional Recursion
content: The n-fold iterated interval integral is defined by recursion on n: base case (n=0) returns f applied to the empty function Fin.elim0; inductive case integrates the outermost variable x₀ from a(0) to b(0) and recurses on the remaining variables via Fin.tail. The four auxiliary lemmas prove the n=0, n=1, n=2 cases explicitly: n=2 gives ∫x∫y f(x,y), recovering the 2D Fubini setup. The @[simp] attribute makes the base and successor cases automatically unfold.
mathContext: Formal definition by structural recursion on $n$: $$\mathcal{I}_{a,b}[f] = \begin{cases} f(\emptyset) & n = 0 \\ \int_{a_0}^{b_0} \mathcal{I}_{\text{tail}(a), \text{tail}(b)}[x \mapsto f(x_0 :: x)]\, dx_0 & n = k+1 \end{cases}$$ where `Fin.tail a : Fin k → ℝ` drops the first component and `Fin.cons x x' : Fin (k+1) → ℝ` prepends $x_0$. This produces the iterated integral $\int_{a_0}^{b_0} \int_{a_1}^{b_1} \cdots \int_{a_{n-1}}^{b_{n-1}} f(x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_{n-1})\, dx_{n-1} \cdots dx_0$.

title: N-Dimensional Order Independence — Axiomatized for General n
content: iteratedIntervalIntegral_order_independent is axiomatized: for any permutation σ of Fin n and any continuous f, the iterated integral equals its permuted version. The 2D and 3D special cases are fully proved (fubini_n2 and triple_fubini_of_continuous). The general case follows the same inductive pattern — peel off the outermost variable, apply the inductive hypothesis inside, use integral_integral_swap for the outer swap — but formalizing this requires Fin-n infrastructure not yet developed.
mathContext: The axiom: for continuous $f : (\mathbb{R}^n) \to \mathbb{R}$ and any permutation $\sigma \in S_n$, $$\mathcal{I}_{a,b}[f] = \mathcal{I}_{a \circ \sigma, b \circ \sigma}[x \mapsto f(x \circ \sigma^{-1})].$$ This says: integrating in the permuted order $(x_{\sigma(0)}, \ldots, x_{\sigma(n-1)})$ gives the same result. The 2D case ($n=2$): proved by `fubini_n2`. The 3D case ($n=3$): proved by `triple_fubini_of_continuous` (for the transposition $(1\,3)$). The general case requires an inductive argument on the length of $\sigma$ as a product of adjacent transpositions — feasible but requiring $\Sigma$-type manipulation over `Fin n`.
